# SEV-1 INCIDENT - RELEASE BLOCKER
**Title:** Statements are filing some payments under the wrong kind of transaction, or dropping the payee name
**Owner:** Payments Operations
**Disposition:** Do not ship this release until it is resolved

## What customers reported

Over the past few days support has collected a run of tickets that all share one
shape: the money itself moved fine, but the app files the payment under a category
that does not match what the customer actually did, or shows the wrong name - or
no name at all - beside it. In every case the row that misbehaves carries one very
particular, uncommon form of raw statement text; everyday rows are labeled exactly
as before. The tickets below are anonymized, but the raw narration each customer
pasted is reproduced verbatim, because that raw text is what makes each case
reproducible.

> "I wrote a cheque against my account and the app just lists it as a general
> transfer now - nothing marks it as a cheque anymore. My earlier cheques were
> tagged correctly. The only thing sitting in that row's note is the cheque's own
> number, nothing else around it."

> "My salary came in and the amount is right, but where my employer's name should
> be the app now just prints the word `NACH`. The raw text on that row looks like
> `ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES` - it used to lift the employer's name off the end
> of that reference, and now it is picking up the wrong piece of it."

> "On some transfers that come in, the sender's name is blank now. Those rows all
> share the same reference layout - a short block of letters, then a long string
> of digits, then the name - for example `GBHDL0123456789 RAVI KUMAR`. The name
> sitting at the end just is not being pulled through anymore; the name column
> comes out empty."

The same batch of complaints also covers two quieter cases that are about the
category rather than the name. The token confirmation charge a bank posts when a
new auto-debit mandate is set up - a small nominal amount, with the note flagging
it as a mandate - is being filed as an ordinary transfer instead of being
recognized as a verification entry. And a refund that came back on a card is
landing as a plain refund for some customers when it should read as a card
reversal; a customer on a different type of account sees the same kind of refund
labeled correctly, so the wrong label appears to depend on the account category.

## Scope of impact

Everyday activity - normal purchases, routine transfers, regular deposits - is
categorized and named correctly, which is precisely why this slipped through QA and
why our monitoring dashboards looked healthy. The breakage is confined to a small
set of unusual transaction forms - among them a note or reference that is exactly
a certain number of digits wide - each one hinging on some exact shape of the raw
row rather than anything about the customer, and each form individually uncommon. But they occur right across the customer base, so they
generate a steady trickle of "why is this labeled wrong" tickets and, more
damaging, they poison the spending-category summaries and payee histories that
several downstream features rely on. That combination is why we are treating it
as ship-blocking rather than a backlog item.

## What we need from engineering

The labeling path is fully deterministic and runs offline - hand it the same
transaction and it reproduces the same wrong answer every time - so each of these
is reproducible on demand and can be pinned down exactly. Get the affected forms
labeling and naming correctly again, and do it without disturbing any transaction
that is already labeled right today. A fix that rescues these cases but nudges the
behavior of ordinary, currently-correct transactions is not acceptable: the pass
condition is simply that the specific problem payments described above come out
right and everything else stays exactly where it is.
I'll investigate the transaction labeling code and the reported failure cases.

# Payment/Transaction Labeling System — Investigation Report

## Architecture overview

This is a Flask microservice (`categorizationapp`) that categorizes Indian bank statement transactions via regex/rule pipelines. **There are no automated tests** in the repo. Git history is a single import commit (`fc21c7f`), so regressions cannot be bisected here.

### Request pipeline (`/categorizeTransaction`)

```
Controller.py
  → AppUtil.clean_input_df()          # strip desc, numeric amount/balance
  → BankScripts/<Bank>.py             # category + partyName extraction
  → [CREDIT_CARD] CardCleanNames + CardPurpose
  → Purpose.py                        # subcategory / merchantType enrichment
  → CleanName.py                      # normalize merchant/payee display names
  → InternalPayment.py                # self-transfers via account holder
  → [SAVING] SalaryDetection.py
  → [optional] PFMCategorization + SimpleDescription
```

**Default category when nothing matches: `"TRANSFER"`** (every bank script uses `np.select(..., default="TRANSFER")`).

### Key file paths (absolute)

| Role | Path |
|------|------|
| API entry / orchestration | `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/Controller.py` |
| DF helpers (`sep_by_dash`, `py_extract`, etc.) | `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/AppUtil.py` |
| Shared bank regexes | `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py` |
| Merchant/purpose regexes | `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/RegexConstants.py` |
| Subcategory / merchant purpose | `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/Purpose.py` |
| Payee name canonicalization | `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/CleanName.py` |
| Category enums | `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/TransactionCategoryEnums.py` |
| Subcategory enums | `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/TransactionSubcategoryEnums.py` |
| Salary heuristics | `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/SalaryDetection.py` |
| PFM mapping | `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/PFMCategorization.py` |
| Per-bank parsers | `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/*.py` (35 banks) |
| CC-specific | `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/CardPurpose.py`, `CardCleanNames.py` |

### How raw statement text is processed

1. Input fields: `description`, `remark`, `amount`, `type` (CREDIT/DEBIT), `balanceAfterTransaction`, plus `bank`, `acc_type`, `accountHolder`.
2. Each bank script runs ordered `np.select` condition lists (first match wins):
   - **Pass 1:** `transactionCategory` (CHEQUE_PAID, AUTO_CREDIT, UPI, REFUND, TRANSFER, …)
   - **Pass 2:** `transactionSubcategory` / `merchantType` (bank-local)
   - **Pass 3:** `partyName` via dash/slash/colon splits and `py_extract`
   - **Pass 4:** partyName cleanup (stop-words, title-case)
3. `Purpose.py` rewrites subcategory from party/description keywords (loans, fuel, salary cues, etc.) and can override category for tax/refund/interest.
4. `CleanName.py` maps noisy party strings to canonical brands (~2000 lines of merchant aliases).

**Important:** `np.select` evaluates all conditions; the **first True** wins. Wrong earlier rules shadow correct later ones.

### Tests

**None found.** No `tests/`, `test_*.py`, pytest/unittest config, or fixtures. Only production package under `/app/categorizationapp/`.

### Recent changes

Only `fc21c7f import codebase` — no incremental history to attribute regressions. Bugs below look like **latent rule defects**, not a recent partial refactor.

---

## Bug-by-bug analysis

### 1. Cheque payments with only a cheque number → general TRANSFER

**Expected:** `CHEQUE_PAID` / `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT`  
**Actual:** `TRANSFER` (default)

**Working banks** (remark is pure digits):
- Axis: `remark ~ ^[0-9]{5,6}$` → cheque  
- BOB, PNB, YES, UCO, BoM, Indusind, Tamilnad: similar remark-digit rules  

**Broken / incomplete:**

**HDFC** (`/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/HDFC.py`):
- Cheque category only if description contains `CHQ`/`CHEQUE`/etc.
- Remark rule exists **only for CREDIT** padded cheque instrument IDs:
  ```python
  # line 100 — CREDIT only
  (remark.len==16) & CREDIT & remark ~ ^[0]{11}[0-9]{5} → CHEQUE_DEPOSIT
  ```
- **No debit-side “remark is cheque number only” rule.** A statement row with description blank/generic and remark `123456` falls to `default="TRANSFER"`.

**ICICI**:
- Needs `CLG` in description or `"CHEQUE"` in remark — pure numeric remark alone is not enough.

**SBI / Canara**: keyword-based only; no pure-digit remark fallback.

**Obvious fix pattern** (already used on Axis/BOB):
```python
[remark.str.contains(r"^[0-9]{3,6}$") & type.eq("DEBIT"), "CHEQUE_PAID"],
[remark.str.contains(r"^[0-9]{3,6}$") & type.eq("CREDIT"), "CHEQUE_DEPOSIT"],
```
Add to HDFC/ICICI/SBI (and any bank missing it). Watch collisions with FD/instrument remarks (PNB already special-cases FD + 6-digit remark).

---

### 2. Salary ACH `ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES` → partyName `"NACH"` instead of employer

**Smoking gun — IDBI** (`/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/IDBI.py` lines 83–86):

```python
["^ACH-BD-NACH", sep_by_dash(description, 2, 3)],  # BUG
["^ACH-BD-",     sep_by_dash(description, 2, 3)],
["^ACH-",        sep_by_dash(description, 1, 2)],
```

Verified split:
```
ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES
→ ['ACH', 'BD', 'NACH', 'ACME INDUSTRIES']
sep_by_dash(2,3) → 'NACH'      # current (wrong)
sep_by_dash(3,4) → 'ACME INDUSTRIES'  # correct
```

**Fix:** use `sep_by_dash(..., 3, 4)` for `^ACH-BD-NACH`.

**Related HDFC salary ACH credit gap** (`HDFC.py` line 154):
```python
^UPI-|^ACH C-  → sep_by_dash(1, 2)
```
For `ACH C-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES` → party becomes **`BD`**, not employer. Debit path has the right pattern (`^ACH D- BD-NACH-` → index 3–4) but **credit `ACH C-` has no BD-NACH special case**.

Category for IDBI `^ACH` CREDIT is correctly `AUTO_CREDIT` (line 14); the bug is **party extraction only**, which then poisons salary detection (SalaryDetection clusters on `partyName`).

---

### 3. `GBHDL0123456789 RAVI KUMAR` → blank sender name

**Smoking gun — IDBI** line 110:

```python
[description ~ "^[A-Z]{5}[0-9]{10,}",
 py_extract(description, pat="[0-9]{10,} (.*)", index=1)]  # BUG: index=1
```

Verified:
- Pattern matches `GBHDL` + `0123456789`
- Regex has **one** capture group → column **0** = `"RAVI KUMAR"`
- `index=1` → `None` → `py_extract` returns `""`

```python
# AppUtil.py
res = description.str.extract(pat=pat).get(index)  # index=1 → None → ""
```

**Fix:** `index=0`.

This is the classic NEFT-style UTR prefix (`[A-Z]{4,5}` bank IFSC-ish + digits + beneficiary name). Same class of narrations may appear on other banks without a dedicated extractor.

---

### 4. Token confirmation / mandate charges → ordinary TRANSFER (or generic CHARGES)

Enums exist:
- `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION`
- `AUTO_MANDATE_CHARGES`

**Coverage is uneven and incomplete.**

| Bank | Mandate charges | Notes |
|------|-----------------|-------|
| Axis, ICICI, SBI, Kotak, PNB, … | Yes | Various `MNDTVRFCHGS` / `E mandate` / `NACH.*CHRG` patterns |
| **HDFC** | **No `AUTO_MANDATE_CHARGES` rules at all** | Soft token folded into generic charges |
| YES | Mandate processing in `CHARGE_YES` → `CHARGES`, not mandate-specific | |

HDFC (`BankRegexConstants.py` line 105):
```python
BANK_CHARGES_HDFC = "...|AMC SOFT TOKEN"
```
→ `CHARGES`, not verification/mandate.

Verification patterns (`BANK_VER`, `BANK_VER_ICICI`, etc.) focus on penny-drop / “validat” / “verif” and **almost always require amount ∈ {1, −1}**. Narrations like “token confirmation”, “soft token”, “mandate registration” without those keywords **miss and default to TRANSFER**.

**BoM type bug** makes verification worse (`BankOfMaharashtra.py` 36–37):
```python
amount.isin(["1","-1"])  # strings
# but clean_input_df() makes amount numeric → never matches
```

**Axis** is aggressive: any CREDIT of amount 1 → `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION` (line 26), which can mislabel real ₹1 credits.

---

### 5. Card refunds → plain REFUND instead of CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL (account-type dependent)

**Indusind** (`Indusind.py` 26–27) — clear logic bug:

```python
POS TXN CREDIT & amount>=10 & accountType=="SAVINGS" → CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL
POS TXN CREDIT & accountType=="SAVING"               → REFUND
```

Controller consistently passes **`SAVING`** (not `SAVINGS`):
```python
if accountType == "SAVING":  # Controller.py, every bank branch
```

So:
- Line 26 (`SAVINGS`) **never fires**
- Line 27 (`SAVING`) always classifies POS credit refunds as **`REFUND`**
- For `CURRENT`, line 95 only sets subcategory `CARD_RECEIPTS`; category still depends on earlier rules

**BankOfMaharashtra** (31–32) uses amount threshold, not account type:
```python
POS TXN CREDIT & amount > 10 → CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL
POS TXN CREDIT               → REFUND   # ≤10 always plain refund
```

**HDFC** (20–21) order issue:
```python
^CRV POS|^POS REF & amount < 25 → REFUND          # first
^POS.*RVSL|^CRV POS|^POS REF    → CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL
```
Small POS reversals permanently labeled `REFUND` because the first rule wins.

**ICICI** (22–23, 30): card reversal needs `RVSL`/`_VPS`/etc. or `^[IV]PS` with amount > 51; many Visa/MC refund strings hit the broad `REFUND` rule instead.

Also: HDFC party extract checks `transactionCategory.isin(["POS Refund","CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL"])` — **`"POS Refund"` is not an enum key** (enum is `POS_REFUND`). Dead branch.

---

## Cross-cutting issues

1. **Default TRANSFER is a catch-all** — any missing keyword/remark rule silently becomes “general transfer.”
2. **`np.select` first-match** — more specific rules must appear *before* broader ones (HDFC ACH C-, HDFC POS refund amount, etc.).
3. **`py_extract` index off-by-one** — easy to ship; only IDBI GBHDL confirmed, worth grepping other `index=1` single-group extracts.
4. **`accountType` string inconsistency** — `SAVING` vs `SAVINGS` (Indusind); string vs numeric amounts (BoM).
5. **No tests** — these SEV-1 cases have nothing to lock behavior.
6. **Purpose.py** can blank subcategory for categories matching `REFUND|...|VERIFICATION` (line 173), so mis-categorization also loses purpose detail.
7. **CleanName.py** only renames known merchants; it does not fix bad segment indices from bank scripts.

---

## Highest-confidence code fixes (for the 5 cases)

| # | File | Change |
|---|------|--------|
| 1 | `BankScripts/HDFC.py` (and ICICI/SBI if needed) | Add remark-only cheque number → `CHEQUE_PAID`/`CHEQUE_DEPOSIT` (mirror Axis/BOB) |
| 2 | `BankScripts/IDBI.py:83` | `sep_by_dash(..., 3, 4)` for `^ACH-BD-NACH` |
| 2b | `BankScripts/HDFC.py:154` | Special-case `ACH C- BD-NACH-` / multi-segment ACH C- like debit path |
| 3 | `BankScripts/IDBI.py:110` | `py_extract(..., index=0)` |
| 4 | `BankScripts/HDFC.py` + `BankRegexConstants.py` | Add `AUTO_MANDATE_CHARGES` / token-confirm patterns; don’t bury soft token only under generic `CHARGES` |
| 4b | `BankScripts/BankOfMaharashtra.py:36-37` | `amount.isin([1, -1])` not `["1","-1"]` |
| 5 | `BankScripts/Indusind.py:26` | `accountType=="SAVING"` (or accept both); reorder so reversal wins over plain refund |
| 5b | `BankScripts/HDFC.py:20-21` | Prefer `CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL` over amount-gated `REFUND` for POS RVSL/REF |

---

## How to validate (no existing tests)

Suggested minimal fixtures per bank:

1. `{remark: "123456", type: DEBIT, description: ""}` → `CHEQUE_PAID`
2. `{description: "ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES", type: CREDIT}` → party `Acme Industries`, category `AUTO_CREDIT`
3. `{description: "GBHDL0123456789 RAVI KUMAR"}` → party `Ravi Kumar`
4. Mandate/token narrations at small amounts → `AUTO_MANDATE_CHARGES` / `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION`
5. `{description: "POS TXN ...", type: CREDIT, acc_type: SAVING}` → `CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL` (not `REFUND`)

I can turn any of these into concrete patches next if you want.
